questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Explore a new culture, which is different from the Danish one and try to have an everyday life in a new country. Moreover, it could be exciting to try university life in another country and improve my English skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really difficult to understand what courses the university offered in English and at what level. Required a lot of correspondence back and forth with the university coordinator to get information on this and response times were long. Also, the university didn't help at all with finding accommodation, so that was also a problem. It was difficult to know where to look for accommodation and what quality the accommodation was.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got information about the semester, the exams etc. The university staff was nice to answer questions about life in Lisbon in general.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The university did not take much initiative to inform, but if you asked the staff, they were nice to give a full answer.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult. It's super hard to see through the possibilities that lie on idealiste, spotahome etc. We ended up googling our way to a landlord. Unfortunately, we were also too late, so we ended up paying a bit more than necessary in rent, but that was our own fault.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start well in advance and ask students who have been there what they lived in and if it is something you can take over.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university did not offer housing, and could not help find housing within the campus

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university mailed an admission form to be filled out. We got it back and the university took care of the rest. Then we got a form where we had to choose subjects and then send it back. The whole process went pretty smoothly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: One could ask questions to the university was during the whole process

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The university did not offer many courses in English, but I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions you get in emails from the university and you'll be fine. Otherwise, ask questions to the staff, they are nice to help and answer, even if the response time is sometimes a bit long.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The university only offered English courses at undergraduate level or LLM, so I took undergratuate courses, so the level was obviously somewhat lower than at the bachelor at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had electives of 2-3 weeks and then exams in the last class or an assignment to take home. Much blackboard teaching with student involvement via handouts.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- EU energy and environmental law
- EU Governance
- EU Internal Market
- Federalism and the EU
- EU competition law
- Property
- Regulation of technology 
- Restorative Justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the courses were interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Higher rent than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was more expensive, and grocery shopping was the same price as in Denmark. Eating at restaurants is cheaper. No books from the university - only pdf documents for reading.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university had 4-5 free excursions during the semester that you could sign up for.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore Portugal's many different cities and landscapes, it's a beautiful country and the people are super hospitable!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Surf all you can. Enjoy the outdoors. Go out for cheap and good food and drinks. Go to Porto, Ericera, Madeira etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, it was. The pace in Portugal is slower than in Denmark, but you soon get used to the fact that you can't do anything about it and just relax in it. Most younger people know English, so you can get around without knowing the language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: All exchange students are there to make new friends and go on trips with other young people. So it comes naturally and everyone is good at taking initiative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None was particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and warmth. Portugal is such a wonderful country and you can learn a lot from it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient. If you're proactive and meet deadlines, things will work out, even if they sometimes work a bit slowly at university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you go on your Master's at KU, don't expect big academic challenges, but go anyway because exchange is so much more than academic.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the good friendships and experiences. It's so cool to try living in another country, like jumping out of everyday life in Denmark. The culture in Portugal is great and there are a lot of cool experiences waiting for you. Don't be afraid to go. You will automatically get in touch with other exchange students who are there for the same reasons.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Be without boyfriend, friends and family for so long. Luckily, Lisbon is no further away than you can visit.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
